result:
Review complete — verdict: **reject**.

The diff itself is well-built (real SUCCESS_CRITERIA re-verification, working regression tests against the actual incident fixture, read-only audit mode), and is correctly classified tier1 (purely additive, no `.github/workflows/**` touched). But it doesn't actually close the incident it claims to fix: the live pipeline that performed today's mass mis-collapse (`/opt/veridian/ai-os/execute_backlog_plan.py` + an untracked pre-fix copy of `plan_backlog_completion.py`, both outside git, both from earlier today) is untouched and still re-runnable — the fixed logic only lives in a new file nothing calls automatically. I also found the new script's own `--apply` path never marks the representative task `completed` as its own action text promises, and a weak `shell=True` command-injection surface in `verify_success_criteria()`. All three are recorded in `review-verdict.json`.
